changes: p1: name normalized to 'Bhairava' with 'ācārya' kept in titles (name had kept the title); confidence lowered to medium because 'Bhairavācārya' may stand for the divine revealer (Bhairava/Śiva), not a human author. The next verse says the tantra came from Śambhu's mouth (śambhor vaktrāgataṃ tantraṃ).
Notes expanded: 'kābdaśāhāni' may hide a date chronogram, but it can't be resolved from the colophon as quoted. The scribes are an unnamed father and son, so no persons were added for them.

notes: The closing verse 'lilekha kābdaśāhānipūrṇṇaṃ putrapitā sahaḥ (!)' says the copy was written by a father together with his son (putra-pitā saha), but neither is named. 'kābdaśāhāni' is corrupt. It may contain a word-numeral chronogram ('abda' = year) or a disguised name, but no reliable year or name can be recovered, so no date or era is given. 'Bhairavācārya' as 'author' may be a conventional attribution to the divine revealer rather than a historical person. The phrase śambhor vaktrāgataṃ tantraṃ ('the tantra that came from Śambhu's mouth') supports this. The NGMCP catalogue fields are empty, so there was nothing to check against.
